# agetime

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/bayesiandemography/agetime/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/bayesiandemography/agetime/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/bayesiandemography/agetime/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/bayesiandemography/agetime?branch=main)
<!-- badges: end -->

Work with age, period, and cohort labels.

**agetime** has functions for validating, manipulating, and harmonising labels, and for extracting information from them. 

One example: filtering on age.

```{r filter}
library(agetime)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)

df <- data.frame(
  age = c("0-14", "100+", "15-39"),
  count = c(100, 40, 200)
)	

df |>
  filter(age_lower(age) >= 15)
```

Another example: standardizing period labels, and inserting missing levels.

```{r clean}
x <-  c("2003 to 2005", "2012--2015", "2000-2005")

x |>
  period_modify_five()

x |>
  period_modify_five() |>
  period_levels_fill() |>
  table()
```

See `?agetime` for a full list of functions grouped by task.
